newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian soymeal rally falters eyeing Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal rally falters eyeing Chinese demand.

text.p: A slight dip in Indian soymeal offers in the past two days has drawn some Chinese buying interest, but regional traders said on Thursday another $10 a tonne cut in prices is needed to spark bigger purchases.
Current Indian offers are now around $310 a tonne C&F China down from over $320 at the start of the week, but the really strong demand is lurking below $300, they said.
Indian exporters said on Friday that they had so far signed contracts for 150,000 tonnes of soymeal for November to December shipment, mainly to China and Indonesia.

But the Chinese appear under no pressure to buy in larger quantities with Hong Kong traders reporting on Tuesday that around 600,000 tonnes of South American and U.S.-origin soymeal was expected to arrive in Chinese ports by mid-September.

Southeast Asian buyers have also largely stayed away from the soymeal market in the face of the Indian rally, although there was talk that Malaysia may now have concluded an anticipated purchase of between 120,000 to 150,000 tonnes for November/December shipment.

Local Indonesian prices have been weighed down by a reported 60,000 tonnes of 44 percent protein Argentine soymeal imported in August, which was quoted at 790 rupiah a kilo compared with 820 rupiah last week. Indian 48 percent protein soymeal was quoted at 805 rupiah a kg.
This year's Indian soybean harvest starting in October is estimated at 4.5 million tonnes, which is about 30-40 percent higher than last year, one western trader said.
